content.title: About
content.content: Mexican pizza is a dish that combines classic Mexican ingredients (ground beef, beans, corn, chili peppers, shredded cheese) with a traditional pizza crust. It is usually topped with tomato sauce, sprinkled with cheese, and baked until golden.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first Mexican pizza recipe appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a taco‑inspired pizza.
The original version uses a sauce seasoned with cumin and paprika for a distinctive aroma.
Mexican pizza is often served with guacamole, sour cream, and fresh cilantro.
Some regions add fried onions and jalapeños for extra heat.
The crust can be made from regular wheat flour or cornmeal for a more authentic flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Ground beef and beans provide essential amino acids for muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomato sauce and meat contain vitamins B6 and B12, important for metabolism.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Beans and corn add dietary fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and chili peppers are high in lycopene and vitamin C, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies iron, magnesium, and potassium, which help heart and muscle function.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese and prepared sauce can be salty, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Jalapeños and chili can irritate the stomach in people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The crust and cheese make the dish energy‑dense, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Mexican pizza hot, sliced into wedges. Add sour cream, guacamole, fresh cilantro, and a squeeze of lime if desired. It pairs well with a light green salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or microwave to retain a crisp crust.
